QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the concentration of dissolved gas in water at 25°C if partial pressure of gas at same temperature is 0.15 atm. $K_H = 0.15 \, \text{mol dm}^{-3} \, \text{atm}^{-1}$

Solution.S:
According to Henry's law:

$$C = K_H \times P$$

Given:

$$K_H = 0.15 \, \text{mol dm}^{-3} \text{atm}^{-1}$$

$$P = 0.15 \, \text{atm}$$

Substituting:

$$C = 0.15 \times 0.15 = 0.0225 \, \text{mol dm}^{-3} = 0.0225 \, \text{M}$$

Thus the correct option is D.
